episode.title: The Fate of Boxer
episode.context: On Animal Farm, the loyal workhorse Boxer has given everything to the revolution. Now, as his strength finally fails, we witness the true nature of the pigs' leadership.
episode.art_style: Watercolor storybook illustration with warm earth tones, visible brushstrokes, pastoral lighting with darker shadows for emotional moments
episode.narrator_style: warm, deliberate storyteller with undertones of sadness

boxer.name: Boxer
boxer.description: A massive carthorse with a white stripe down his nose, enormously powerful but now showing signs of age. His coat is less shiny than before, his great haunches somewhat shrunken. He wears a determined expression despite obvious exhaustion.

clover.name: Clover
clover.description: A stout motherly mare approaching middle age, with kind eyes and a gentle demeanor. Her brown coat is well-groomed despite hard work, and she moves with careful, nurturing purpose.

benjamin.name: Benjamin
benjamin.description: An elderly donkey with a cynical expression, gray around the muzzle. He is the oldest animal on the farm and rarely shows emotion, preferring to observe in silence.

squealer.name: Squealer
squealer.description: A small fat pig with round cheeks, twinkling eyes, and a shrill voice. He moves with quick, nimble movements and has a way of skipping from side to side when making a point.

napoleon.name: Napoleon
napoleon.description: A large, fierce-looking Berkshire boar with a reputation for getting his own way. He carries himself with authority and is always accompanied by his dogs.

windmill.name: The Windmill
windmill.description: A partially rebuilt stone structure on a knoll, representing the animals' endless labor. Piles of stone surround its base, evidence of years of backbreaking work.

farmhouse.name: The Farmhouse
farmhouse.description: A comfortable dwelling where the pigs now live exclusively. Warm light glows from its windows while the other animals sleep in the cold barns.

van.name: The Knacker's Van
van.description: A large enclosed van drawn by two horses, with sinister lettering on its side reading 'Alfred Simmonds, Horse Slaughterer and Glue Boiler, Willingdon.'

sentences: After the battle for the windmill, life on Animal Farm grew harder than ever.
The animals had won, but at a terrible cost, and now they faced another bitter winter with even less food than before.
scenes.video_description: A wide view of Animal Farm in early winter, frost covering the fields. The damaged windmill stands in the background, partially rebuilt. Animals move slowly across the frozen ground, their breath visible in the cold air.
scenes.camera_style: Wide establishing shot, slowly panning across the farm

sentences: Boxer, the great workhorse, had injured his hoof in the battle.
But he refused to rest, not even for a single day.
scenes.video_description: Boxer pulling a heavy cart loaded with stones, his injured hoof wrapped in cloth. Despite the obvious pain, his expression remains determined as he strains against the harness.
scenes.camera_style: Medium shot focusing on Boxer's determined face, then tilting down to his bandaged hoof

sentences: Every evening, he would quietly tell Clover that his hoof troubled him greatly.
She treated it with herbs she had chewed into poultices, begging him to work less hard.
scenes.video_description: Inside a dim stable at evening, Clover tenderly applies herb poultices to Boxer's hoof. A single lantern casts warm light on their faces as she looks up at him with concern.
scenes.camera_style: Intimate close-up shot, warm lighting

sentences: A horse's lungs do not last forever, she warned him.
But Boxer had only one dream left: to see the windmill completed before his retirement.
scenes.video_description: Boxer gazes out the stable door toward the distant windmill silhouetted against a sunset sky. His eyes reflect both weariness and unwavering hope.
scenes.camera_style: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind Boxer, looking toward the windmill

sentences: You see, when Animal Farm was first created, the animals had promised themselves a better life.
Retirement pensions had been agreed upon: five pounds of corn daily for horses, hay in winter, and perhaps an apple on holidays.
scenes.video_description: A dreamlike vision of an idyllic pasture corner, with an older horse resting peacefully under a tree. Apples and hay surround him, sunlight dappling through leaves.
scenes.camera_style: Soft focus, dreamy lighting, gentle camera drift

sentences: Boxer's twelfth birthday, his retirement age, was due in late summer.
He imagined peaceful days spent learning to read, finally mastering the alphabet he had struggled with for so long.
scenes.video_description: Boxer in the stable, looking at letters painted on the wall: A, B, C, D. He mouths the letters silently, a gentle smile on his tired face as he imagines a quieter life.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on Boxer's face, then panning to the letters on the wall

sentences: But while Boxer dreamed of retirement, the reality of the farm was growing darker.
Rations were cut again and again, except for the pigs and their guard dogs.
scenes.video_description: A contrast shot: on one side, thin animals receiving meager portions of grain; on the other, plump pigs eating from overflowing troughs. The divide is stark and cruel.
scenes.camera_style: Split composition shot, contrasting the two groups

sentences: Squealer, the pigs' spokesman, always had an explanation.
He called the cuts 'readjustments,' never 'reductions,' and insisted things were far better than in the old days under Farmer Jones.
scenes.video_description: Squealer standing on a raised platform, gesturing dramatically to a crowd of thin, attentive animals. He holds papers covered in statistics, his small eyes twinkling as he speaks.
scenes.camera_style: Low angle shot making Squealer appear important, then cutting to the confused faces of the other animals

sentences: He read out long lists of figures proving they had more oats, more hay, better water than ever before.
The animals believed him, mostly because they could barely remember how things used to be.
scenes.video_description: Close-up of Squealer's mouth moving rapidly, papers fluttering. The scene shifts to show sheep and hens nodding along, their empty food bowls visible in the foreground.
scenes.camera_style: Quick cuts between Squealer's animated speaking and the hungry but nodding animals

sentences: Besides, they told themselves, at least they were free now.
They were no longer slaves to humans. That had to count for something.
scenes.video_description: Animals huddled together in a cold barn, their breath visible. Despite their thin frames, they look at each other with a kind of stubborn pride, a tattered flag with a hoof and horn visible on the wall.
scenes.camera_style: Warm but melancholy medium shot of the gathered animals

sentences: Meanwhile, Napoleon had fathered thirty-one piglets with the farm's sows.
A special schoolroom was being built just for them, and they were forbidden from playing with the other young animals.
scenes.video_description: Young piebald piglets march in a line through the farmhouse garden, their snouts in the air. In the background, young lambs and foals watch from behind a fence, excluded.
scenes.camera_style: Tracking shot following the privileged piglets, then cutting to the watching farm animals

sentences: New rules appeared constantly.
All other animals must now step aside when a pig approached on the path, and pigs were given the privilege of wearing green ribbons on Sundays.
scenes.video_description: A muddy farm path where a thin cow quickly moves aside as a portly pig with a green ribbon struts past. The pig doesn't even glance at the cow.
scenes.camera_style: Eye-level shot emphasizing the power dynamic

sentences: The farm needed money badly, so more and more was sold off.
The hens had to give up six hundred eggs a week, barely leaving enough to hatch new chicks.
scenes.video_description: Sad-eyed hens watching as a pig collects their eggs into large baskets. One hen tries to protect her nest but is shooed away.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on the hens' distressed faces

sentences: Rations were cut in December, then cut again in February.
The lanterns in the animals' stalls were forbidden to save oil.
scenes.video_description: Dark, cold stables where animals shiver in complete darkness. Through a window, the warm glow of the farmhouse is visible in the distance.
scenes.camera_style: Dark interior shot with the farmhouse light visible through the window

sentences: But the pigs seemed comfortable enough. In fact, they were putting on weight.
One afternoon, a delicious smell drifted across the yard from the old brew-house.
scenes.video_description: Steam and appetizing smells waft from a small building. Hungry animals lift their noses, sniffing hopefully. Their ribs show through their coats.
scenes.camera_style: Shot following the visible steam and smell across the yard to the hopeful animals

sentences: The animals wondered if a warm mash was being prepared for their supper.
But no warm mash appeared. That Sunday, it was announced that all barley would now be reserved for the pigs.
scenes.video_description: Disappointed animals standing before empty feeding troughs as the announcement is made. In the background, pigs can be seen entering the farmhouse with satisfied expressions.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot capturing the collective disappointment

sentences: Soon the news leaked out: every pig was now receiving a daily ration of beer.
Napoleon himself got half a gallon, always served in a fancy soup tureen that had once belonged to Farmer Jones.
scenes.video_description: Napoleon drinking from an ornate porcelain tureen, foam on his snout. The dining room is warm and comfortable, a stark contrast to the cold barns outside.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on Napoleon's indulgent drinking, then pulling back to show the luxurious setting

sentences: To make up for the hardships, Napoleon invented something called Spontaneous Demonstrations.
Once a week, the animals would march around the farm in military formation, celebrating their glorious revolution.
scenes.video_description: A procession of animals marching in formation around the farm. Pigs lead the way, followed by horses, cows, sheep, and poultry. Dogs flank the parade, keeping everyone in line.
scenes.camera_style: Tracking shot following the parade, then aerial view showing the rigid formation

sentences: Boxer and Clover always carried a green banner between them reading 'Long live Comrade Napoleon.'
There were poems in Napoleon's honor, speeches by Squealer, and sometimes the gun was fired in celebration.
scenes.video_description: Boxer and Clover holding a large green banner between them as they march. Despite their weariness, they participate dutifully. Squealer stands on a platform, gesturing dramatically.
scenes.camera_style: Focus on the banner bearers, then cutting to Squealer's animated speech

sentences: If anyone complained about the marching, the sheep would drown them out with bleating: 'Four legs good, two legs bad!'
But somehow, these celebrations helped the animals forget their empty bellies, at least for a while.
scenes.video_description: Sheep bleating loudly in unison, their mouths wide open. Other animals nearby look tired but manage small smiles as flags flutter and the gun fires in the background.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on the sheep, then pulling back to show the full celebration

sentences: In April, Animal Farm was declared a Republic, and they needed to elect a President.
There was only one candidate. Napoleon was elected unanimously.
scenes.video_description: Napoleon standing on a raised platform as animals raise their hooves and paws in the air. A crude ballot box sits nearby, completely unnecessary given there's only one name on the ballot.
scenes.camera_style: Low angle shot of Napoleon looking imperious, then wide shot of the 'voting' animals

sentences: On that same day, new revelations about Snowball were announced.
The pig who had been expelled years ago was now said to have fought alongside the humans all along, leading their forces with the cry 'Long live Humanity!'
scenes.video_description: Squealer holding up official-looking documents, pointing to fabricated evidence. The animals gasp and mutter, their memories of the past growing hazier.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on the fake documents, then reaction shots of confused animals

sentences: That summer, Moses the raven returned to the farm after years away.
He still told the same stories about Sugarcandy Mountain, a paradise where animals would rest forever after death.
scenes.video_description: A black raven perched on a tree stump, wings spread dramatically as he preaches to a gathering of weary animals. Above him, clouds part to suggest a heavenly vision.
scenes.camera_style: Low angle shot of the raven against the sky, then reverse shot of the listening animals

sentences: Up there, just beyond the clouds, he promised, there were fields of clover and linseed cake growing on hedges.
Many of the tired, hungry animals believed him. After all, wasn't it right that a better world should exist somewhere?
scenes.video_description: A dreamy vision of Sugarcandy Mountain: lush green fields, trees bearing treats, animals resting peacefully in eternal sunshine. The image wavers like a mirage.
scenes.camera_style: Soft focus dream sequence, slowly fading back to reality

sentences: The pigs called his stories lies, yet they let Moses stay on the farm.
They even gave him a daily allowance of beer, asking nothing in return.
scenes.video_description: Moses the raven drinking from a small dish of beer while a pig looks on with a knowing smirk. The other animals work in the background, too busy to notice this arrangement.
scenes.camera_style: Medium shot capturing the curious tolerance between pig and raven

sentences: After his hoof healed, Boxer worked harder than ever before.
All the animals worked like slaves that year, rebuilding the windmill and building the schoolhouse for the young pigs.
scenes.video_description: Boxer straining to pull an enormous boulder up a slope toward the windmill. His muscles bulge, veins standing out, but his coat is dull and his ribs are beginning to show.
scenes.camera_style: Low angle shot emphasizing the enormous effort, stone looming above

sentences: Sometimes the long hours on so little food were almost unbearable.
But Boxer never faltered, never complained.
scenes.video_description: Boxer continuing to work as the sun sets, then rises, then sets again. Time-lapse showing his tireless dedication while other animals rest and return.
scenes.camera_style: Time-lapse sequence showing Boxer's unending work

sentences: Nothing he said or did showed that his strength was failing.
But his hide had lost its shine, and his great haunches seemed to have shrunk.
scenes.video_description: A comparison shot showing Boxer from before and now. His magnificent frame has diminished; his eyes, though still determined, carry a deep weariness.
scenes.camera_style: Side-by-side dissolve showing Boxer's physical decline

sentences: The others said he would pick up when the spring grass came.
But spring came, and Boxer grew no fatter.
scenes.video_description: Spring flowers blooming around Boxer as he works, but he remains thin and tired. The beauty of the season contrasts painfully with his deteriorating condition.
scenes.camera_style: Bittersweet composition of spring beauty and physical decline

sentences: Sometimes, pulling boulders up the quarry slope, it seemed only his willpower kept him standing.
His lips would form the words 'I will work harder,' but he had no voice left to speak them.
scenes.video_description: Extreme close-up of Boxer's face straining with effort, his lips moving silently. A single tear tracks through the dust on his cheek as his legs tremble beneath him.
scenes.camera_style: Intimate close-up capturing the silent determination

sentences: Clover and Benjamin begged him to take care of himself.
But Boxer wouldn't listen. His twelfth birthday was approaching, and he wanted to leave a good store of stone before his retirement.
scenes.video_description: Clover and Benjamin standing before Boxer, their expressions pleading. Boxer shakes his great head gently, then turns back to his work with quiet stubbornness.
scenes.camera_style: Three-shot showing the emotional exchange

sentences: Then, late one summer evening, a terrible rumor spread across the farm.
Something had happened to Boxer.
scenes.video_description: Twilight falls over the farm. Animals stop what they're doing, their ears pricked, passing urgent whispers from one to another. The windmill looms ominously in the background.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot with animals freezing mid-action, tension building

sentences: He had gone out alone to haul stone to the windmill.
Two pigeons came racing back with the news: Boxer had fallen and couldn't get up.
scenes.video_description: Two pigeons flying urgently across the darkening sky, their wings beating frantically. Below, an overturned cart is visible near the windmill, a large shape lying motionless beside it.
scenes.camera_style: Following the pigeons' flight, then revealing the scene below

sentences: Half the animals on the farm rushed to the knoll where the windmill stood.
There lay Boxer between the shafts of his cart, his neck stretched out, unable even to lift his head.
scenes.video_description: Animals gathered in a horrified semicircle around Boxer's fallen form. He lies in the traces of his cart, sides heaving, a thin stream of blood trickling from his mouth.
scenes.camera_style: Slow push-in toward Boxer's prone body through the gathered animals

sentences: His eyes were glazed and his sides were matted with sweat.
Clover dropped to her knees beside him, crying his name.
scenes.video_description: Clover kneeling beside Boxer's head, her eyes filled with tears. She nuzzles him gently while other animals stand in shocked silence around them.
scenes.camera_style: Intimate ground-level shot of Clover and Boxer

sentences: It is my lung, Boxer whispered. It does not matter.
I think you will be able to finish the windmill without me. There is a good store of stone accumulated.
scenes.video_description: Close-up of Boxer's face as he speaks weakly, his breath labored. Behind him, the pile of stones he has gathered stands as testament to his life's work.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on Boxer's face, gentle focus shift to the stone pile

sentences: I had only another month to go anyway, he said. I had been looking forward to my retirement.
Perhaps Benjamin and I could have retired together and been companions.
scenes.video_description: Benjamin standing silently near Boxer's head, using his long tail to keep flies away. His usually impassive face shows deep emotion for perhaps the first time.
scenes.camera_style: Two-shot of Benjamin and Boxer, emphasizing their friendship

sentences: Someone ran to tell Squealer what had happened.
The pig arrived full of sympathy and concern, announcing that Napoleon was making arrangements to send Boxer to the hospital in town.
scenes.video_description: Squealer trotting importantly to the scene, his face arranged in an expression of concern. He gestures reassuringly to the worried animals as he delivers his message.
scenes.camera_style: Medium shot of Squealer arriving, reaction shots of relieved animals

sentences: The animals felt uneasy about this. No animal except Mollie and Snowball had ever left the farm.
But Squealer convinced them that the veterinary surgeon could help Boxer better than anyone on the farm could.
scenes.video_description: Worried animals exchanging uncertain glances as Squealer speaks. Some nod reluctantly, trusting in the pigs' wisdom despite their misgivings.
scenes.camera_style: Reaction shots of various concerned animals

sentences: With difficulty, Boxer was helped to his feet and limped back to his stall.
Clover and Benjamin prepared a good bed of straw for him there.
scenes.video_description: Boxer being supported by other animals as he limps slowly toward the barn. Clover and Benjamin walk on either side of him, steady and supportive.
scenes.camera_style: Slow tracking shot following the painful journey to the barn

sentences: For two days, Boxer rested in his stall while Clover gave him medicine twice a day.
In the evenings, she lay beside him and talked softly while Benjamin kept the flies away.
scenes.video_description: A warm scene inside the stable: Boxer lying on clean straw, Clover administering pink medicine from a bottle. Soft evening light filters through the wooden slats.
scenes.camera_style: Gentle, warm interior shot emphasizing care and companionship

sentences: Boxer said he wasn't sorry for what had happened.
If he recovered, he still had three good years ahead of him, and he would finally have time to learn the rest of the alphabet.
scenes.video_description: Boxer looking peaceful despite his weakness, gazing at the letters painted on the stable wall. His expression is hopeful as he imagines a future of rest and learning.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on Boxer's hopeful face, letters visible in soft focus behind

sentences: But Clover and Benjamin could only visit after working hours.
And it was in the middle of the day when the van came to take Boxer away.
scenes.video_description: A large enclosed van pulling into the farm yard, dust rising from its wheels. The afternoon sun casts long shadows as two horses draw the ominous vehicle closer.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot of the van approaching, building tension

sentences: The animals were working in the fields when they saw Benjamin running toward them.
It was the first time anyone had ever seen the old donkey gallop.
scenes.video_description: Benjamin galloping wildly across the field, his usual slow demeanor completely abandoned. His eyes are wide with panic as he brays loudly.
scenes.camera_style: Tracking shot following Benjamin's urgent gallop

sentences: Quick! Quick! he shouted. They're taking Boxer away!
Without waiting for orders, all the animals raced back to the farm buildings.
scenes.video_description: Animals dropping their tools and running toward the farm. Sheep, pigs, hens, and horses all streaming in the same direction with desperate urgency.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot of the stampede toward the farm

sentences: There in the yard stood a large closed van with a sly-looking man on the driver's seat.
Boxer's stall was empty.
scenes.video_description: The van standing in the yard, a man in a bowler hat holding the reins. The stable door stands open, straw scattered as if from a struggle. Animals gather around in confusion.
scenes.camera_style: Ominous shot of the van, then cut to the empty stall

sentences: The animals crowded around the van calling out their goodbyes.
But Benjamin pushed through them, shouting: Fools! Do you not see what is written on the side of that van?
scenes.video_description: Benjamin forcing his way to the front of the crowd, stamping his small hoofs in fury. He points desperately at the writing on the van's side.
scenes.camera_style: Dynamic shot of Benjamin's frantic warning

sentences: In a deadly silence, Benjamin read the words aloud.
Alfred Simmonds, Horse Slaughterer and Glue Boiler. They are taking Boxer to the knacker's!
scenes.video_description: Extreme close-up of the painted letters on the van's side: 'Alfred Simmonds, Horse Slaughterer and Glue Boiler, Willingdon.' The words seem to grow larger, more horrifying.
scenes.camera_style: Slow zoom on the lettering, letting the horror sink in

sentences: A cry of horror burst from all the animals.
At that moment, the man whipped his horses and the van began to move.
scenes.video_description: Animals recoiling in shock, mouths open in cries of protest. The van lurches forward, wheels beginning to turn as the driver cracks his whip.
scenes.camera_style: Rapid cuts between horrified animals and the departing van

sentences: Clover forced her way to the front and tried to run after the van.
Boxer! she cried. Get out! They're taking you to your death!
scenes.video_description: Clover running desperately after the van, her stout legs straining. Her mouth is open in a terrible cry, tears streaming down her face.
scenes.camera_style: Following shot of Clover's desperate chase

sentences: All the animals took up the cry: Get out, Boxer! Get out!
And then Boxer's face appeared at the small window at the back of the van.
scenes.video_description: Boxer's white-striped face appearing at the tiny window, his expression confused and weak. Behind him, the farm animals are receding as the van picks up speed.
scenes.camera_style: Shot from inside van showing Boxer's face at window, animals visible behind

sentences: Then his face disappeared, and there came a tremendous sound of drumming hooves from inside.
Boxer was trying to kick his way out.
scenes.video_description: The van shaking violently from impacts within. Dents appear in the wooden sides as Boxer kicks desperately, the sound echoing across the farmyard.
scenes.camera_style: External shot of the van shaking, emphasizing the futile escape attempt

sentences: Once, a few kicks from Boxer's hooves would have smashed the van to matchwood.
But his strength had left him, and the drumming of hooves grew fainter and died away.
scenes.video_description: The kicks growing weaker, the van's shaking subsiding. The vehicle continues down the dusty road, the sounds of struggle fading to silence.
scenes.camera_style: Slow motion shot of the van driving away, sound fading

sentences: The animals begged the horses pulling the van to stop, crying out: Don't take your own brother to his death!
But those horses were too ignorant to understand, and they only quickened their pace.
scenes.video_description: The two draft horses pulling the van, their ears set back, moving faster. Farm animals run alongside crying out, but the van horses don't even turn their heads.
scenes.camera_style: Split focus between pleading farm animals and indifferent draft horses

sentences: Someone thought to close the gate, but it was too late.
The van passed through and disappeared down the road. Boxer was never seen again.
scenes.video_description: The five-barred gate swinging shut a moment after the van passes through. The vehicle grows smaller in the distance, finally disappearing around a bend in the road.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot of the van vanishing, gate closing on emptiness

sentences: Three days later, Squealer announced that Boxer had died peacefully in the hospital.
He claimed to have been at Boxer's bedside during his final hours.
scenes.video_description: Squealer standing before the assembled animals, a false tear on his cheek. His voice is dramatic as he delivers the news, one trotter raised theatrically.
scenes.camera_style: Medium shot of Squealer performing his grief

sentences: Boxer's last words, Squealer said, were: Forward, comrades! Long live Animal Farm! Long live Comrade Napoleon!
Napoleon is always right. Those were his very last words.
scenes.video_description: Close-up of Squealer's face as he delivers the fabricated last words, his small eyes watching the audience carefully for any sign of doubt.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on Squealer's calculating expression

sentences: Then Squealer addressed the rumor about the van.
Some animals, he said indignantly, had jumped to the foolish conclusion that Boxer was being sent to the knacker's.
scenes.video_description: Squealer's demeanor changing, becoming defensive and sharp. He paces back and forth, his tail swishing with irritation.
scenes.camera_style: Tracking shot following Squealer's agitated movements

sentences: The explanation, he said, was simple: the van had once belonged to the knacker but was now owned by the veterinary surgeon.
The old name simply hadn't been painted out yet. That was how the mistake had arisen.
scenes.video_description: Animals listening to the explanation, some nodding slowly, wanting to believe. Others exchange uncertain glances, but no one dares to speak up.
scenes.camera_style: Reaction shots of animals accepting the lie

sentences: The animals were enormously relieved to hear this.
Squealer went on to describe the expensive medicines Napoleon had paid for, and their sorrow was tempered by the thought that at least Boxer had died happy.
scenes.video_description: Relief spreading across the animals' faces as they accept the comfortable lie. Some even smile through their tears, grateful for the false comfort.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot of the animals' relieved expressions

sentences: Napoleon appeared the following Sunday to deliver a speech in Boxer's honor.
He reminded everyone of Boxer's two favorite sayings: I will work harder, and Napoleon is always right.
scenes.video_description: Napoleon standing on a raised platform, delivering his oration with practiced authority. A wreath of laurels sits nearby, supposedly sent to Boxer's grave.
scenes.camera_style: Low angle shot of Napoleon speaking, emphasizing his authority

sentences: These maxims, Napoleon said, every animal would do well to adopt as their own.
The pigs announced they would hold a memorial banquet in Boxer's honor.
scenes.video_description: Napoleon gesturing grandly as he concludes his speech. Behind him, other pigs nod solemnly, already looking forward to the promised banquet.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot capturing Napoleon's performance and the pigs' anticipation

sentences: On the day of the banquet, a grocer's van delivered a large wooden crate to the farmhouse.
That night, the sounds of singing and quarreling came from within, followed by a tremendous crash of glass.
scenes.video_description: Night scene of the farmhouse, windows glowing warmly. Shadows of celebrating pigs move behind curtains. The sound of breaking glass shatters the quiet.
scenes.camera_style: Exterior night shot of the farmhouse with sounds of revelry

sentences: No one stirred in the farmhouse until noon the next day.
And the word went round that from somewhere, the pigs had acquired the money to buy themselves another case of whisky.
scenes.video_description: Morning light on empty whisky bottles outside the farmhouse. In the background, thin animals begin their day of labor while the farmhouse remains silent.
scenes.camera_style: Dawn shot revealing the aftermath, contrast between pigs' indulgence and animals' labor

sentences: And so Boxer, the strongest and most loyal worker Animal Farm had ever known, was gone.
He had given everything he had to the revolution, worked until his body broke, and dreamed of a retirement he would never see.
scenes.video_description: A ghostly image of Boxer superimposed over the windmill he helped build. His form fades slowly as the windmill stands silent against the sky.
scenes.camera_style: Ethereal dissolve of Boxer's image over his life's work

sentences: The pigs had sold him for whisky money, and told the animals comforting lies about veterinarians and hospital beds.
And the animals believed them, because believing was easier than facing the terrible truth.
scenes.video_description: Clover and Benjamin standing together at the fence, looking toward the road where the van disappeared. Benjamin's usually cynical face shows profound grief.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot of the two friends in silent mourning

sentences: I will work harder, Boxer had always said. Napoleon is always right.
But in the end, all his work and all his loyalty meant nothing to those who had promised to take care of him.
scenes.video_description: Close-up of Boxer's empty stall, straw still pressed where he lay. His worn harness hangs on a hook, swaying slightly in the breeze.
scenes.camera_style: Slow pan across the empty stall, lingering on the abandoned harness

sentences: This is the story of how power corrupts, and how those in charge can betray the very creatures who trust them most.
And it is the story of Boxer, who deserved so much better than the end he received.
scenes.video_description: Final wide shot of Animal Farm at sunset. The windmill stands completed, but the farm feels empty. A single white stripe of cloud crosses the sky, echoing Boxer's white-striped face.
scenes.camera_style: Slow pull back to wide establishing shot, fade to black
